title: Add Captions to YouTube Shorts (Burned-In)
metaDescription: Burn captions into YouTube Shorts so every viewer sees them, CC button or not. Automatic transcript, five styles and a 9:16 MP4 export.
h1: Add burned-in captions to YouTube Shorts
intro: Shorts viewers swipe fast, often with the sound low. Burned-in captions are on screen from the first frame, without anyone pressing CC. Supertitle transcribes your Short, lets you fix the text and exports a 9:16 MP4.
summary: Captions on screen from the first frame, no CC button needed.

safeZone.description: On a Short, YouTube places its controls, channel name and title over the video, toward the bottom and along the right side, and some of its interface near the top. The editor's Safe zones overlay shows roughly where that is on a full-screen vertical video; captions in the Bottom position are kept clear of it.

faq.question: Why burn captions in if YouTube has its own?
faq.answer: YouTube's captions are closed: viewers have to turn them on. Burned-in captions show for everyone, and they look the way you styled them.

faq.question: Can I turn a clip from a long video into a Short?
faq.answer: If you have the clip as a file, yes: upload it, trim the start and the end, and crop it to 9:16. Supertitle doesn't pick clips out of long videos for you.
